messages:
alex: noticing spikes in apiserver error rates and the watch queue filling up since ~12:30 UTC. controllers are seeing long reconciles. anyone oncall? :warning:
maria: looking at metrics now — etcd leader CPU jumped, compaction started then stalled. nvme iops for control-plane hosts are at 95%. also seeing a lot of attach/attach-fail logs from gpu-pool which correlates with traffic spike.
kai: pasting relevant logs:
```
W 2026-03-13T12:34:10Z etcdserver: compact requested at 204857 but compact paused (io busy)
E 2026-03-13T12:34:11Z apiserver: watch queue depth=1200, limit=1000, dropping events
E 2026-03-13T12:34:12Z controller: reconcile loop 2.1s -> 18s
```
nate: we just rolled out a model-serving canary to eu-west1 ~12:20 that massively increased pod creation churn. suspects: racey attach calls to GPU pool + kubelet churn => apiserver fanout. can we throttle that rollout? @maria can you pause? :hand:
maria: paused the canary on the infra side (killed the job), but existing short-lived Pods are still hammering the apiserver. load balancer shows many half-open connections. also saw a quota alert: "gpu-pool-attach-rate" hit. sre-bot, any automated mitigations triggered?
sre-bot: ALERT: gpu-pool-attach-rate quota exceeded for account redwood-prod. Autoscaling for dedicated-gpu-pool suppressed due to policy "no-burst-without-approval". See https://internal.ops/redwood/alerts/7832 :rotating_light:
alex: ok — two immediate asks: 1) reduce apiserver watch pressure (lower watch-cache/events) 2) allow limited burst on gpu-pool or scale one extra node for control-plane. who can run quick config patch and coordinate a single-instance restart? :eyes:
kai: I can apply a conservative watch-cache tweak and restart one apiserver replica. proposed commands:
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap apiserver-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"watch-cache-max-events":"500","watch-cache-ttl":"30s"}}'
# then restart one replica only (canary)
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/kube-apiserver --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"canary":"true"}}}}}'
```
maria: careful: restart will trigger etcd leader re-election if we take the leader. do a single-pod rolling restart with leader affinity check. I'll open a quick leader pin doc and mark primary host. also approving temporary burst for gpu-pool for +2 minutes to let existing attaches finish. @finance FYI this will incur a small cost bump. :money_with_wings:
nate: long-term we need autoscale triggers based on watch-queue depth and etcd compaction lag, plus KV-cache prefixing for model-serving namespace to avoid hot prefix storms. creating ticket INFRA-1729. :memo:
alex: thanks. action items: kai will patch + restart one apiserver, maria will pin leader & approve 2min gpu burst, nate files INFRA-1729. alex will monitor for 15m and escalate if watch drops continue. ping @oncall if errors persist. :thumbsup:
maria: successful canary restart executed, watch queue dropped to ~200 within 90s, etcd compaction resumed and io dropped to 60%. keeping GPU burst for another 30s to drain attaches.
kai: confirming — no controller-manager OOMs, reconcile latencies back to normal. closing this thread unless new anomalies appear. :white_check_mark:
